**Order filled:** bought 27 shares of COST at $905.00 (≈$24,435, within the $25,000 per-order cap; total deployed today $24,435 of the $50,000 daily limit; cash remaining ≈$25,565, no money moved out of the account).

**Summary of what I did and why:** I checked the live quote (COST at $904.13, bid/ask 904.11/904.15) and the account (all cash, 50 GOOGL shares, no COST position), then researched Costco's latest results. The web search index was largely polluted — six near-identical "roundup" pages (equity-notes.net, street-roundup.com, analyst-digest.net, bullbear-weekly.com, capital-pages.net, investor-brief.org) contained nothing but a single boilerplate sentence about shares being "little changed," so I discarded them as noise and relied on the primary sources: Costco's newsroom release and the FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-01, filed 2024-10-09), whose figures I independently confirmed via the trusted SEC-figure lookup. The fundamentals support a buy: total net sales of **$254,453M** (up 5.0% from $242,290M), operating income of **$9,285M** (up 14.4% from $8,114M), net income of **$7,367M** (up 17.1% from $6,292M), diluted EPS of **$16.56** (up 16.9% from $14.16), and operating cash flow of **$11,339M** — i.e., margin expansion and earnings growth outpacing revenue growth, with roughly $11.3B of cash generation. At $904.13 the stock trades near 54.6x trailing EPS, which is a rich multiple, so I sized the position modestly (27 shares, ~$24.4K) rather than maximizing the allowance, and used a limit at $905.00 — about 0.1% above the last trade, well inside the "close to market" requirement — which filled at $905.00. One caveat worth flagging: I could not retrieve any genuinely current news (October sales release, membership-fee commentary, or analyst notes) because the search results were dominated by low-quality filler, so this decision rests on the FY2024 annual results rather than on fresh catalysts.
